THE ROW WAS THE BUILD'S OWN ERROR AND THE PROOF CAUGHT IT: authoring builder-aider turned test_route.py's equality assertion red, and the FIRST reading of that red here was that the assertion had gone stale and should be widened to admit a fourth kind of row. That is the plaster the deterministic-red rule exists to stop, and it got one step from being applied. Akien's ruling, 2026-08-16, verbatim: "no. absolfuckinglutely no. The inference proxy knows about providers and models. it does not understand about consumers. the consumer asks for what it wants. period, end of story." The red was correct and the build was wrong; the equality was RESTORED, not loosened, and the row removed (8 deletions in stacks/domains.json).

THE WHY BENEATH THE RULING, and it is why this cannot recur as a special case — Akien, 2026-08-16, verbatim: "if the inference proxy knows about consumers, then there is no need for domains. and then the inference proxy becomes extremely complicated. That's why this is a no. we already know that when a single component gets very complicated, all levels of claude begin to have trouble". The row is SELF-COLLAPSING: admit one caller-named row and every caller earns one, at which point a vertical stops meaning a shape of ask and starts meaning a class of consumer — the domains stack becomes a consumer registry and there was never a reason to have domains at all. This is falsifier tell 6 from the stack's own authoring ticket ("rows are FIELD SETS an instance composes, never classes it belongs to") tripped by a build that had the sentence in front of it. The second half is a MEASURED cost that generalizes past this proxy: complexity concentrated in one component degrades every tier of Claude working on it.

THE FENCE HAS NO HOLDER RIGHT NOW, and that is stated rather than papered over. The removed row was the only money-fence between the chat verb and a paid provider. Under the ruling the fence belongs to the consumer — the shim asks for hex and qwen3-coder:30b by name, and asking for exactly that IS the safety — but the shim is not built. So between now and the aider-shim build, nothing structural stops a chat request naming an expensive model; the general default and the models stack are all that stand. Carried forward on tickets/aider-shim.json as a build obligation.
